composers_checked.note: fr.wikipedia's instrumental list (duos, Op. 2 trios, several sets of quatuors concertants, quartets on known airs) shows nothing else recorded; the only recordings found are historic LPs (Loewenguth 1959, Pascal 1939), so confidence is medium

composers_checked.name: Vachon, Pierre
composers_checked.note: Gap check from en/fr Wikipedia (Op. 1 violin sonatas, Op. 4 trios, Op. 5 and Op. 7 quartets, Op. 9 lost, Op. 11). Op. 5 No. 1 in A is on the Auvidis disc; MusicBrainz lists a quartet 'Op. 5 No. 3 in F minor' with the same movement titles but other timings, so the Op. 5 numbering is uncertain (not added twice)

composers_checked.name: Rigel, Henri Joseph
composers_checked.note: en/fr Wikipedia work lists (symphonies, keyboard sonatas and pieces, oratorios, operas, quartets Op. 10) show no other chamber work; the six Op. 10 quartets are the only recorded ones

composers_checked.name: Hoffstetter, Roman
composers_checked.note: The six Op. 3 quartets (formerly Haydn's Op. 3, Hob. III:13-18; the attribution to Hoffstetter dates from the 1960s); en.wikipedia lists no other works. Timings from Kodály and Melos recordings (MusicBrainz, Apple Music)

composers_checked.name: Paisiello, Giovanni

composers_checked.name: Kuhlau, Friedrich

composers_checked.name: Salieri, Antonio
composers_checked.note: Both kept works rest on one documented professional concert (Berlin Philharmonic members, 4 March 2026); no recording (Apple Music, MusicBrainz, web) and no modern edition were found, hence low confidence. Wikipedia's list adds only fugues for two or three instruments and a lost guitar set

note: Slice c42 (Dalayrac, Vachon, Rigel, Hoffstetter, Exaudet, Paisiello, Pla, Soler, Rosetti, Kuhlau, Salieri): all 39 candidate pages are kept or skipped. Floor evidence is mostly Apple Music track lists, MusicBrainz, IMSLP and Wikipedia; Presto and the Naxos Music Library were not reachable and Apple's search endpoint answered 403 for a while late in the run. (1) Dalayrac and Vachon's Op. 11 are known only from 1939-59 LPs: the Loewenguth Quartet's Archiv disc (Dalayrac 'Op. 1 No. 5' = Op. 7 No. 5, Op. 7 No. 3; Vachon Op. 11 Nos. 1 and 5) and the Quatuor Pascal; confidence medium. (2) Paisiello Op. 23: two key schemes (IMSLP and Ferrarini D, G, G, C, G, G; Robinson, Brilliant and Aulicus C, D, E minor, G, G, G); titles follow IMSLP, the R. number and the other key are in aka. (3) Hoffstetter Op. 3 are the benchmark's set; no benchmark issue (recorded timings of No. 5 run 9-14 minutes). (4) Kuhlau Op. 51 No. 2: discs say E major, IMSLP E minor with an E-major introduction. (5) Soler: year 1776 (IMSLP 1766); minutes average two discs that differ by up to ten minutes. (6) Added from the gap check: Vachon's Op. 5 No. 1 (Auvidis, 1996) and Exaudet's Concerto à cinq instruments (Audax ADX 13782, 2021; one to a part per the Classical Music review; a violin concerto, so say if the owner wants it out). Not added: Vachon's quartet labelled Op. 5 No. 3 in F minor on MusicBrainz; Rosetti quartets D6-D8, D15, D17, Flute Quartet D16 and Notturno B24 (a 2013 Deutsche Harmonia Mundi disc named only in Wikipedia's Murray table; not found); Paisiello's nine string quartets (no recording found). (7) Salieri's Scherzi and Fugue pass only on a Berlin Philharmonic concert (4 March 2026); the owner may prefer to drop them.
